Last time, I tried on fedora 21, I must say I had no success and reinstalled the OS several times. The last version as of now is 352.21, it's stable for Linux 64. To give more details I use a Lenovo E540. Did anyone had any success ? And if yes, how?

Edit: grammar
How to install GeForce GT 740M display driver?
Ok so it worked, but a piece of advice for other. in bios for display config need to be selected the nvidia GPU, other ways Linux wont see it even if in windows the driver will now to activate it.

After some reading, it is possible that you don't even need to use bumblebee on Lenovo e540, it has the bios option to use the integrated GPU or 'dedicated' ( in laptops the GPU is not really dedicated but let's say so ... ). So if you select Nvidia and install the default driver it should work by default at full capacity. Keep in mind that the battery life will lower, because a much more power consumption. After i did the install of bumblebee and activated from bios the nvidia GPU, when i run optirun nvidia-smi I only get the Nvidia one and for the intel it says is not supported.

Edit: If anyone needs some help with this, just ask here!

Is your setup ONLY the Nvidia card, or do you have an "Optimus" setup with an Intel card? If you have an Optimus setup, it may be easier to disable the Intel card in BIOS to only use your Nvidia card. Bumblebee is still a bit touchy :(

This is true, as I had massive problems with Bumblebee a few months ago trying to put Fedora on one of my laptops. I ended up having to just disable the Intel on board and use Nvidia.

That did wonders for the battery life /s.
